label: PILOT EDITION
title: Three things worth knowing
subtitle: Verified progress in health, nature and society.

stories.title: Malaria vaccines are reaching routine childhood programmes across Africa
stories.text: Two WHO-recommended vaccines are now being introduced through national immunisation programmes, adding a new layer of protection alongside nets, medicines and testing.
stories.why: WHO expects vaccination in Africa to save tens of thousands of young lives every year.
stories.source: World Health Organization · updated 4 Dec 2025 · link checked 21 Sep 2026

stories.title: The Iberian lynx has moved back from the brink
stories.text: After two decades of conservation, the wild population grew from just 62 mature animals in 2001 to more than 2,000 lynx in Spain and Portugal in 2023.
stories.why: The species was reclassified from Endangered to Vulnerable — proof that long-term habitat and breeding work can reverse decline.
stories.source: Reuters, reporting the IUCN assessment · 20 Jun 2024 · link checked 21 Sep 2026

stories.title: Far fewer children die before their fifth birthday than a generation ago
stories.text: The global under-five mortality rate has fallen by more than half since 2000, driven by vaccines, nutrition, safer births and treatment for preventable disease.
stories.why: Millions more children now survive their earliest years, even as progress remains uneven and needs protecting.
